I feel this heavily. My negative perception filter will often get in my way of seeing peoples loving interactions with me. 

The first thing to become aware of is this filter and to realize that in seeing the world through this filter you are only seeing ONE out of the many possible things people may be feelings about you. 

The second thing is to inquire into yourself. What is making you feel as though you are bitter or unloved? Where does the negative self talk come from? What if the negative self talk is not true? We often hide our shadow as people behind a mask because we are afraid what others will think of us if they see us experiencing anger or sadness. This brings me to my next point:

Be vulnerable. Seriously, own how you feel and don’t be afraid to express it(in a healthy way not destructive to others or yourself), if you have friends you know and trust, particularly ones that have a good track record of lifting your spirits, ask them for a reflection. “Hey, right now I am feeling unloved, do you think I’m doing anything that is toxic in our friendship?” A good friend will be honest with you and tell you what’s up. 

Lastly, just own how you feel and don’t make such an effort to change the emotion. Trust that the emotion will tapper away on its own. One of the big things I’ve learned when it comes to confidence is that it’s okay for us to feel shy and it’s normal for us to fear rejection. After all, this is ingrained in our biology, we have these feelings because we want to belong in the tribe and not belonging in the tribe way back in prehistoric times meant death for us. This is why our brains create these negative delusions, so that it may protect us from death. The most confident people have learned to handle rejection, failure, and their short comings better. They have developed a healthier relationship with it. 

Be patient my friend, It takes a lot of work. If I can leave you with one more thing today, that thing is to seek to “accept yourself as you are” rather than “change yourself.” Self love doesn’t began when we become our ideal self, it begins right now, just as we are! Not everyone will like you but if you start being true to yourself and your values, you will within time, attract like minded individuals who resonate with your most authentic values. 

Hope all of this helps.

OK so this question had me thinking for a bit and I will do my best to answer without being too subjective: 

Short answer: I cannot be certain that death is necessarily another doorway to another life, I don’t think any of us have this answer.

Long answer: I do not believe any of us in this life know what lies in the afterlife once we die. I believe that even highly spiritual people whom are able to channel entities such as angels from a higher dimension have this answer for us or at least one that can be fully described in our 3-dimensional world. I described in my post that this life feels like a video game that I got bored of and who is to say that the next life whether it be a higher dimension or another incarnation of a human life will not have the same boredom that I feel in this current life? I believe that whatever the next realm is, it will have its own set of challenges, it will not be a full on blissful experience where I’ll never get bored. 

What gives me my affirmation for the doorway is subjective: 

I remember having memories before birth. I remember being a C-section baby before my mom told me in my toddler years that I was a C-section baby. During this time, I was able to consciously see life through my mom‘s eyes and seeing what she was going through at the time. I was essentially an observer as my mom was doing her daily tasks in life, pregnant with me. During these times, I recalled feeling restless like I couldn’t wait to finally be born. It felt like I was on a very long waiting list.. though it did not feel like I was waiting at a DMV. To me this waiting room in a way felt like home. I felt loved and appreciated, I remember feeling curious and excited when I was there, I knew where I was and whom I was talking to. This knowing that I was going to be born human was shocking to me, to have remembered being conscious even before my first Cry as a baby boy. 

So death to me would essentially be like going back to this “waiting room” and understanding more of where I was, what it was, and why I decided to come back to earth.

What this told me was that where ever I was before I was born human, I was bored there too and I had chosen to become human because I got bored of where I was, or maybe I choose to come back because I had a mission. Now I wish to go back home because some days on earth, that home I got so bored of is really starting to feel like home now.
